$comment: English display overlay for the labels (§218) of this package of the Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan (DECISION-0070). The file is not compiled into the CLIR and is read only by the presentation layer (verbalize --labels, the MCP resource law://<package>/verbalized/en, the workbench). The translation is a working one made by the formaliser from the Russian labels of the package, checked against the authentic Russian and Kazakh texts of the Constitution; it is not an official publication, hence the status "translation" for every entry. Spelling is British. A key is the local name of the declaration (the part of the node id after "#").

CommissionEstablished.text: Article 59, paragraph 1. The Kurultai forms commissions

ConstitutionalEarlyTermination.text: Article 52, paragraph 3. Early termination of powers requires a ground and a procedure provided for by the Constitution

ConstitutionalLawTwoThirds.text: Article 61, paragraph 3. Constitutional statutes are adopted by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the votes of the total number of the deputies of the Kurultai

ConstitutionalVetoOverride.text: Article 56, sub-paragraph 2). Objections of the President to a constitutional statute are overridden by a majority of three-quarters of the votes of the total number of the deputies

DeputyCandidateEligibility.text: Article 54, paragraph 3. A deputy of the Kurultai may be a citizen of the Republic who has attained the age of twenty-five and has permanently resided in Kazakhstan for the last ten years

DeputyDetentionException.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. The detention of a deputy is permissible where he is detained at the scene of a crime, where a grave or especially grave crime has been committed, or with the consent of the Kurultai

DeputyDetentionGroundConsent.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. The consent of the Kurultai is a ground lifting the protection of a deputy

DeputyDetentionGroundGraveOffence.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. The commission of a grave or especially grave crime is a ground lifting the protection of a deputy

DeputyDetentionGroundInTheAct.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. Detention at the scene of a crime is a ground lifting the protection of a deputy

DeputyImmunity.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. A deputy of the Kurultai may not be detained without the consent of the Kurultai, except where detained at the scene of a crime and where a grave or especially grave crime has been committed

DeputyInviolabilityApplies.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. The protection of a deputy against detention operates so long as none of the three grounds named is present

DeputyInviolabilityApplies/unless/0.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. The protection of a deputy against detention operates so long as none of the three grounds named is present

DeputyPersonalImmunity.text: Article 55, paragraph 3. A deputy of the Kurultai may not be detained without the consent of the Kurultai, except where detained at the scene of a crime and where a grave or especially grave crime has been committed

DeputyTermExpiry.text: Article 53, paragraph 2. The term of office of deputies of the Kurultai is five years

FinancialBillWithGovernmentOpinion.text: Article 60, paragraph 6. A bill reducing revenue or increasing expenditure is introduced only where there is a positive opinion of the Government

FirstSessionThirtyDays.text: Article 58, paragraph 2. The first session of the Kurultai is convened not later than thirty days after the day the election results are published

Government.text: Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

GovernmentMemberDismissalRequest.text: Article 56, sub-paragraph 17). On the initiative of not less than one-third of the deputies, the Kurultai, by not less than two-thirds of the votes, takes a decision to apply to the President for the release of a member of the Government

GovernmentNoConfidence.text: Article 56, sub-paragraph 13). On the initiative of not less than one-fifth of the deputies, the Kurultai, by a majority of the total number of the deputies, passes a vote of no confidence in the Government

Kurultai.text: Kurultai of the Republic of Kazakhstan

KurultaiChairElection.text: Article 57, paragraph 1. Election of the Chair by secret ballot by a majority of the total number of the deputies

KurultaiChairMayConveneAndPreside.text: Article 57, paragraph 3. The Chair convenes sittings and presides over them

KurultaiChairMayDirectAgendaPreparation.text: Article 57, paragraph 3. The Chair exercises general direction of the preparation of the matters before the Kurultai

KurultaiChairMayEnforceRules.text: Article 57, paragraph 3. The Chair ensures compliance with the Rules of Procedure of the Kurultai

KurultaiChairMayIssueOrders.text: Article 57, paragraph 5. The Chair issues orders on matters within his competence

KurultaiChairMaySignActs.text: Article 57, paragraph 3. The Chair signs the acts of the Kurultai

KurultaiChairRemovalOrResignation.text: Article 57, paragraph 2. Recall or resignation of the Chair by a majority of the total number of the deputies

KurultaiPowersEndAtNewConvocation.text: Article 52, paragraph 2. The powers end when the first session of the new convocation begins its work

KurultaiPowersStartAtFirstSession.text: Article 52, paragraph 2. The powers of the Kurultai begin with the opening of its first session

KurultaiResolution.text: resolution of the Kurultai or of one of its working bodies

LawPresentedWithinTenDays.text: Article 60, paragraph 5. A statute adopted by the Kurultai is submitted for signature to the President within ten days

MissedReconsiderationAcceptsObjection.text: Article 56, sub-paragraph 2). Failure to observe the one-month time limit for reconsideration means that the objections of the President are accepted

OrdinaryLawMajority.text: Article 61, paragraph 4. Statutes are adopted by a majority of the votes of the total number of the deputies of the Kurultai

OrdinaryVetoOverride.text: Article 56, sub-paragraph 2). Objections of the President to a statute are overridden by a majority of two-thirds of the votes of the total number of the deputies

PresidentialFinancialBillException.text: Article 60, paragraph 6. For bills introduced by the President, an opinion of the Government is not required

PriorityBillDue.text: Article 60, paragraph 2. A priority bill must be adopted within two months

PriorityBillTwoMonths.text: Article 60, paragraph 2. A priority bill adopted not later than the day the two-month period ends has been adopted in time

RepeatedAbsenceSanction.text: Article 55, paragraph 1. The absence of a deputy without good reason more than three times entails the application of the sanctions laid down by statute

RepeatedChairRefusalAllowsDissolution.text: Article 57, paragraph 1. A repeated refusal to elect the Chair entitles the President to dissolve the Kurultai

Report.text: report of a member of the Government to the Kurultai

SessionQuorumTwoThirds.text: Article 58, paragraph 5. A sitting of the Kurultai is competent where not less than two-thirds of the total number of the deputies are present

StandingCommitteeEstablished.text: Article 59, paragraph 1. The Kurultai forms standing committees, whose number is determined by a constitutional statute

TrustVoteTimingAndAnnualCap.text: Article 60, paragraph 7. The vote on the question of confidence is held not earlier than forty-eight hours after the question is raised, and the power is used not more than twice a year

WorkingBodyResolutionWithinCompetence.text: Article 59, paragraph 2. Committees and commissions issue resolutions within their competence
